language.name: Gekapiso
language.scope: Original source compilation; no simulated evolution or reconstructed daughter-language forms
language.representation: Source romanization; case, accents, hyphens and source variants retained

usage.concept_lookup: semantic_aliases maps concise English keys to concepts and lexicon IDs; concepts retain source glosses. english_gloss_index indexes complete gloss strings.
usage.speech_act_lookup: speech_acts maps communicative intent to attested lexicon entries, relevant grammar rules, examples and optional slot templates.
usage.status_policy: attested/explicit are source-backed; inferred describes analysis of examples; unspecified means the original evidence does not supply a form. Editorial IDs, domains and speech-act categories are not original terminology.
usage.generation_policy: Use attested expressions first. Apply explicit grammar only within its documented scope. Do not generate original-language realizations for unspecified acts or resolve conflicts silently.
usage.null_policy: null construction means no supported realization template, not a zero marker.
usage.reference_policy: Source lines are one-based in the embedded raw Markdown. Lexeme and concept IDs are stable for this source snapshot, not across source edits.
usage.lexicon_scope: All nonblank vocabulary and expression rows in the selected original glossary tables, digit forms, and selected heading vocabulary. Remaining examples, names, affixes and table patterns are preserved in raw_source and grammar; this is not an exhaustive token dictionary.
usage.analysis_policy: Part-of-speech and domain labels are editorial. A slash/comma gloss is preserved intact rather than treated as a formal ontology. Repeated forms retain separate source entries.

sources.role: Original handwritten native-script chart, visually inspected
Original handwritten shortening rule, visually inspected

identify.semantic_intent: State who or what an entity is, including its name.
identify.note: The act label and slot template are analytical; no dedicated verb meaning identify is listed.

inform.note: Declarative examples support informing. No dedicated inform marker is specified.

request.semantic_intent: Ask someone to provide something or perform an action.
request.note: Bekende means to beg, not a separately attested general verb to request.

offer.semantic_intent: Propose giving something or doing something for an addressee.
offer.note: These are related concepts (give, help, ability), not attested equivalents of offer. No original offer formula or dedicated lexeme is documented.

refuse.semantic_intent: Decline a request, invitation or offer.
refuse.note: An is attested as no/not; its use as a refusal is a pragmatic inference. Anbede denotes inability, which is not necessarily refusal.

promise.semantic_intent: Commit the speaker to a future action.
promise.note: No promise lexeme or conventional commitment formula is documented. Future tense alone does not establish a promise.

ask.note: Question constructions are documented; a dedicated verb to ask is not listed.

warn.semantic_intent: Alert an addressee to a possible danger or adverse event.
warn.note: Harm, hurt, death and fear are related lexical concepts, not attested warning formulas. No dedicated warn form is documented.

deny.semantic_intent: Reject the truth of a proposition or give a negative answer.

request_permission.semantic_intent: Ask whether the speaker may perform an action.
request_permission.note: The attested examples use -za on the second verb despite the general infinitive-chain rule; they are retained exactly.

word_order.description: Subject-verb-object is an observed declarative order, not an explicitly stated universal rule.
word_order.qualification: Questions and commands have different patterns; no complete constituent-order specification is given.

pronoun_omission.description: Pronouns can be inferred; source examples omit recoverable subjects and sometimes objects.

verb_stems.description: Remove final -de from a regular infinitive to obtain the stem.
verb_stems.qualification: Do not silently regularize inconsistent attested examples.

tense.description: Add the listed ending to a regular verb stem. Immediate/distant are source categories without defined clock-time boundaries.

paradigms.source_label: Distant Present; in the process of

ing_forms.description: The source labels these -ing forms and says they do not go after bozo.
ing_forms.qualification: No distant-present -ing ending is listed. The source does not fully explain the overlap with -zoki.

verb_chains.description: Use a conjugated verb followed by an infinitive.

negation.description: An means no/not. Examples show separate An before a predicate, An before a whole clause, An after bozo, and joined an- forms.
negation.qualification: Scope and spacing are not governed by one explicit rule; do not equate all patterns mechanically.

never.description: The source glosses clause-initial an plus a distant past/future verb as never.
never.qualification: This construction-specific gloss does not make every distant tense intrinsically negative.

content_questions.description: The source says to add a- for a question and lists question words; the practice section attests Akien.
content_questions.qualification: Aten, Awai and Ao already begin with a; prefix behavior for these forms is unspecified. Do not automatically produce aaten, aawai or aao.

polar_questions.description: The source gives (V+na»Qword)(+PN?) and examples with a verb plus na plus an optional pronoun.
polar_questions.qualification: Bezonake contains present bezo; Wanenake is also attested, without -zo. A single mandatory tense-marking rule for questions is not established.

formal_questions.description: Zí introduces formal questions, including requests for permission.

commands.description: Use De, a verb in -ze, and an optional target.

possession.description: Attach -ko to the possessor; the source writes possession as ~ in symbols. Attested possessors precede the possessed noun.
possession.qualification: Source spellings magika and Emirianako are retained; no spelling correction is implied.

number_and_demonstratives.description: The noun heading gives -lo for plural; pronouns, demonstratives and other examples use -ro.
number_and_demonstratives.qualification: No conditioning rule distinguishes -lo from -ro. Do not choose a universal plural ending.

articles_and_quantifiers.description: The source lists definite, indefinite and quantity words.

relations.description: Prepositions and the descriptive linker nu are listed in the source.
relations.qualification: Ne is glossed of but also appears with from in practice examples; de has multiple functions.

modification.description: Descriptive words can precede nouns with nu; some examples omit nu.
modification.qualification: A universal requirement for nu is not documented.

nominalization.description: Verb stems take -e for a conceptual noun, -en for a gerund noun, or -kari for one that performs the action.

verbal_adjectives.description: The source gives Le plus a verb in -za or -zon, with nu before a described noun in examples.
verbal_adjectives.qualification: The source specifies -zon as the only -ing adjective form; passive-like readings also occur in Se bozo roveza, but no general passive rule is stated.

adverbs_and_degree.description: De plus a verb-derived form in -na describes a verb; adjective degree endings are -to and -tas, and -kan is glossed -ly.

attribution.description: De plus an optional personal form and a property expresses an abstract quality.

coordination_and_clauses.description: Listed conjunctions connect clauses or phrases; kari introduces that/relative content, tokari means because, and aten introduces when clauses in examples.
coordination_and_clauses.qualification: Airi is glossed if/maybe; a full conditional construction is not given.

lexical_time.qualification: Temporal-adverb placement is attested but not exhaustively specified.

names.description: Name order is family name, middle name(s), given name. Name formation combines the first two tandems of describing words.
names.qualification: Examples include shortenings and spelling adjustments; no fully deterministic transformation is specified.

language_names.description: -iso is given for spoken/written language names.

numbers_and_dates.description: The source supplies digit stems, place-value suffixes, Le X for ordinals, and míu/díu plus a number for dates.
numbers_and_dates.qualification: Numeral examples shorten -cin/-con to -ci/-co; the 17 gloss at line 1065 conflicts with akacin amon and the 18 gloss at line 1071. Preserve rather than normalize.

singular_consonants.others: Romanized as consonant, written as shortened consonant+u character

accentuation.qualification: No more detailed phonetic or stress interpretation is supplied.

shortening.qualification: Handwritten romanized captions are transcribed with ordinary letter case; native glyphs remain in the PDF.

native_script.description: Handwritten chart with A/U/E/I/O rows and consonant columns; consult the source PDF for exact glyph shapes.

C0272.label: To expresss through creation or art

C0428.label: Glory / very high honor and fame

C0706.label: with their species / according to their kind

C0938.label: May I have some water? (Most formal)

L0272.source_gloss: To expresss through creation or art

L0428.source_gloss: Glory / very high honor and fame

L0525.form: Re Uniteza nu Stero Ne Amerí

L0706.source_gloss: with their species / according to their kind

L0938.source_gloss: May I have some water? (Most formal)

source_issues.description: Noun plural -lo is stated; -ro occurs in pronouns, demonstratives, headings and kauro.
Bezonake, bezona(ke), and Wanenake coexist; a- application to already a-initial question words is unspecified.
An is separate or joined and appears in several positions.
Permission examples use necinoza/munkaza although verb chains are described as conjugated verb plus infinitive.
Kama is glossed village, mountain and year; keep separate senses.
Kau/cau, Magia/magika, Arinke/Alinke and Stero/stelo occur; they are not automatically merged.
To wish and To pray have blank source forms. A Jesus row is blank alongside an Apadive entry.
Both -zoki and -zon receive ongoing readings without a complete distinction.
Place suffixes vary in examples, and akacin amon is translated as both 17 and 18.
Gne bozo ometas is glossed That was delicious, despite listed demonstratives and present-tense bozo.
Me doezo de se meko rovezo is preserved; rovezo is used for my love despite the separately stated conceptual-noun ending -e.
The alphabet PDF contains handwritten glyphs; no Unicode character mapping is provided. Romanization is preserved without inventing glyph codes.
Offer, promise and warn are semantic categories supplied by the request, with no dedicated original realization found.

# Gekapiso Language Compilation  
## 0: Alphabet/Pronunciation (Itezaiso/Pie)  
  
  
(See alphabet file)  
  
  

| Name In Gekapiso | Symbol (English)     |
| ---------------- | -------------------- |
| Pidiwe           | ! (Exclamation Mark) |
| Jawe (Ja)        | . (Period (Dot))     |
| Ceniwe           | ? (Question Mark)    |
| Kowero           | “” (Quotation Marks) |
| Atawe            | , (Comma)            |
| Atako            | ‘ (Apostrophe)       |
| Akahiwe          | - (Hyphen)           |
| Furuslau         | / (Forward Slash)    |
| Bakusrau         | \\ (Back Slash       |
| Jajawe           | : (Colon)            |
| Játawe           | ; (Semi-Colon)       |
| Paretesí         | ( ) (Parenthesis)    |
| Ampane           | & (Ampersand / And)  |
| Ner              | @ (At symbol)        |
  
Accentuation Rules:  

| AA » Á (Any vowel)  |  |
| ------------------- | - |
| AiA»AYA (Any vowel) |  |
|                     |  |
  
Shortening Rule: (see file)  
  
Basic Letter Conversions:  

| GEKAPISO Consonant | Spoken Sound Made |
| ------------------ | ----------------- |
| C[*]               | Ch                |
| Q[*]               | Sh                |
| X[*]               | th-s              |
| Z[*]               | Z, (Z[i]: Zhi)    |
  
QXZ example:  

| (Gekapiso written) | (Sound made) |
| ------------------ | ------------ |
| Qa                 | Sha          |
| Xa                 | Th-sah       |
| Za                 | Za           |
  
Vowels:  

| (Vowel) | (Sound Made) |
| ------- | ------------ |
| [aA]    | ah           |
| [uU]    | oo           |
| [eE]    | eh           |
| [iI]    | ee           |
| [oO]    | oh           |
  
Singular Consonants:   

| (Consonant) | (Sound Made) |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [nN] | has the “n” sound in “un” |
| [vV] | has “vb” sound and is extremely staccato (like a STOP or something [like in “gustav”]) |
| (?![nNvV])([a-zA-Z]) | Romanized as “\\g1”, but written as character “\\g1u” shortened |
  
****1: Language Basic Grammar****  
  
Pronouns: (Can be inferred)  

| GEKAPISO | ENGLISH                 |
| -------- | ----------------------- |
| Me       | I                       |
| Se       | You                     |
| Ke       | You (formal/respectful) |
| Ge       | It/He/She (They)        |
| Mero     | We                      |
| Sero     | Y’all                   |
| Kero     | Y’all (formal)          |
| Gero     | They                    |
  
Possessive Pronouns and Adjectives:  

| Meko   | My/Mine                |
| ------ | ---------------------- |
| Seko   | Your/Yours             |
| Keko   | Your/Yours (formal)    |
| Geko   | His,Her(s),Its         |
| Meroko | Our/Ours               |
| Seroko | Your/Yours (p.)        |
| Keroko | Your/Yours (p. formal) |
| Geroko | Their/Theirs           |
  
Possession:  

| -ko / ~                | ‘S               |
| ---------------------- | ---------------- |
| (written ~ in symbols) |                  |
| Ex: Emirianako hihie   | Emiliana’s foods |
| Masonko magika         | Mason’s magic    |
  
Demonstrative Adjectives:  

| Gan(ro) | This (These) |
| ------- | ------------ |
| Gen(ro) | That (Those) |
  
Demonstrative Pronouns:  

| Gán   | This one   |
| ----- | ---------- |
| Gánro | These ones |
| Gén   | That one   |
| Génro | Those ones |
  
Direction:  

| Upa   | Up/Over          |
| ----- | ---------------- |
| Una   | Down/Under       |
| Hurur | Forward/In front |
| Bakur | Backward/Behind  |
| Ure   | Left             |
| Ura   | Right            |
| Nur   | North            |
| Sur   | South            |
| Ís    | East             |
| Ás    | West             |
  
Position:  

| Imaki   | Here/Near           |
| ------- | ------------------- |
| Imoki   | Far                 |
| Imo     | There               |
| Imomoki | Over There          |
| Upa Imo | Over There          |
| Upapu   | Top, Surface, Face  |
| Unamu   | Bottom, Floor, Feet |
| Panarea | Center              |
  
Articles:  

| Re    | The  |
| ----- | ---- |
| A     | A    |
| Aro   | Some |
| Ayo   | All  |
| Anaka | None |
  

| Nák  | Nothing    |
| ---- | ---------- |
| Yón  | Everything |
| Tóru | Anything   |
  
Question Words (Add a- for ?):  

| Kien               | Who               |
| ------------------ | ----------------- |
| Kari               | What, That, Which |
| Kimo               | Where             |
| Aten               | When              |
| Awai               | Why               |
| Ao                 | How               |
| Tokari             | Because           |
| (V+na»Qword)(+PN?) |                   |
| Ke bezo            | You can.          |
| bezona(ke)         | Can (you)?        |
  
Confirmations and Negations:  

| Ai           | Yes             |
| ------------ | --------------- |
| Airi         | If, Maybe       |
| An           | No/Not          |
|              |                 |
| Ex.          |                 |
| An bezo dide | Not able to die |
  
Prepositions:  

| Ne     | Of                      |
| ------ | ----------------------- |
| Nu     | Describing another word |
| De     | About, over, supercede  |
| Ner    | On, in ,at              |
| Nenen  | Off, out, away          |
| Nenato | From                    |
| Nedan  | Onto, into, to          |
  
Coordinating Conjunctions:

| ------ | --- |
| Tane   | And |
| Tenore | Nor |
| Tebuke | But |
| Tsore  | Or  |
| Tyete  | Yet |
| Tsoe   | So  |
  

| Tantan | Also                           |
| ------ | ------------------------------ |
| Dek    | Again                          |
| Zí     | With; (formal questions)       |
| Vresi  | Like (comparing inhuman items) |

| Necinode | To leave                            |
| Piode    | To pronounce                        |

| Epresíde | To express                          |

| Krinade  | To clean                            |
| Conde    | To count                            |
| Kenvide  | To party, celebrate                 |
| Bidade   | To breathe                          |
| Kramade  | To classify, group, divide          |

Multiple verbs rule:  

| (Conj. + Inf.)   |                |
| ---------------- | -------------- |
| Ke bezo made ge. | You can do it. |
| Bezonake made ge | Can you do it? |
  
Verbs(present tense):  

| -zo    | (Immediate Present)                   |
| ------ | ------------------------------------- |
| -zoki  | (Distant Present) (in the process of) |
| bozo   | am/is/are                             |
| bozoki | am being, is being, are being         |

| ------ | ---------------------- |

| ------ | ------------------ |

****3.3 Nouns - Names (Nauro - Nomiaro)****  
  
Name Ordering:  
  
Family names are seen like family titles, so they come first when stating your name. Middle names are like personal titles, so they appear next, then your given name.  
  
Obtaining Names:  
  
Take the first two tandems of each describing word and combine:  
Ex: Chaney   
-> lived around oak trees  
-> Biredo(house) / kyapo(oak tree)  
-> Bire/kya   
-> Birekya  
  
Ex. Weston  
-> a western settlement  
-> Ás(west) / Bkaman(town)  
-> Ás/bka  
-> Ásbuka
